row.case: FGFR3-TACC3 urothelial carcinoma, one patient's record, the fusion's 5' partner
row.approved: erdafitinib (small molecule, pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor), FDA accelerated approval 12 April 2019 and conversion to full approval 19 January 2024 for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with susceptible FGFR3 genetic alterations, determined by an approved companion diagnostic (therascreen FGFR RGQ RT-PCR) whose susceptible alterations include the FGFR3-TACC3 fusion; no antibody against FGFR3 is approved
row.why: the structural call is the measurement that selects the patient, as the amplification is for trastuzumab, so a pipeline that cannot read a caller's own fusion export misses every patient the label is written for; and the fusion's 5' partner is the arrangement where the product keeps the gene's own N-terminus, so the curated surface figure describes a protein that may or may not be the one the tumour makes and the score has to say so rather than answer 0.0 or read the annotation at full value
row.mechanism_reach_reason: no modelled modality is established against this target; the nearest is blocking_antibody at compatibility 0.25 with surface_accessible unanswered, which is a question and not an option
row.alteration_magnitude_reason: no copy count is present in this patient's data; no variant allele fraction was reported; no observed position to look up, so hotspot status does not apply. Absent quantities are absent and are not imputed
row.verdict: correctly not a surface target; approved drug is out of scope

note: The eleventh benchmark case, registered on 2026-10-10 before it was run (therapeutic_sv_case_registration) and added to the benchmark's case list whatever the outcome. Three quantities are scored apart, as the benchmark scores them: whether the target is recovered, whether the route is called correctly, and whether the mechanism ranked first is defensible. The ten existing rows are the regression guard and are re-scored offline with the structural-variant reader as it was before this lane's change and as it is now. A recovered target is a retrospective consistency with what is already approved for the alteration, never evidence that a therapy works.

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
